findings.text: The batch fermented from 1.088 to 0.992; the creator calculated 12.96% ABV.

evidence.passage: We started at 1.088 ... minus our final gravity of 0.992 ... times 135 ... gives us 12.96.

findings.text: Taste before making post-fermentation adjustments.

evidence.passage: The next step of this really does require us to know what it's going to taste like.

videos.title: Let's Drink MEAD! Orange Creamsicle Mead One Year Tasting
videos.creator: City Steading Brews

findings.text: After one year, the backsweetened mead was reported at 1.028 and described as dessert-sweet.

evidence.passage: This is at 1.028 final gravity. So, this is sweet, almost pretty much a dessert mead ... sitting for a whole year.

findings.text: The tasters reported that aging made it smooth and mellow and that orange, vanilla, and honey remained perceptible.

evidence.passage: It's really nice. It's really smooth and mellowed.
Good orange ... added a little vanilla ... taste all the components. It tastes wonderful.

videos.title: STABILIZERS in MEAD Making at Home: Mistake?
videos.creator: City Steading Brews

findings.text: The creators frame chemical stabilization and pasteurization as tools and do not claim the single comparison settles all recipes.

evidence.passage: This was just the simplest mead ever ... not a definitive test ... it will be different in other recipes.
I'm not telling you never do this ... These are all tools.

findings.text: In this batch, they identified the chemically stabilized samples by a different smell and an acrid, bitter-rind taste; other differences were subtle.

evidence.passage: If I drank one now and another one in 15 minutes, I probably wouldn't know which was which.
The flavor was different, the smell was different ... the taste has an acrid kind of thing.

visual_review_needed: Confirm blind-sample labels during the reveal.

videos.title: Fermentation Fundamentals - More Yeast Is NOT the Answer!
videos.creator: City Steading Brews

findings.text: Use unchanged gravity readings one week apart, rather than bubbles alone, to judge stability.

evidence.passage: Wait a week, take another reading. If those two readings don't change, it's done ... stable.

findings.text: For the discussed sluggish step-fed fermentation, they advised waiting before adding more yeast and considering removal of oak until conditioning.

evidence.passage: Sluggish fermentation ... I told him to sit back and wait ... I probably would not have put more yeast in yet.
Let it go for a while ... if not, I would probably get those wood chips out ... put them in secondary.

videos.title: What Homebrew Fermentation Should Look Like -CSB Unpasteurized
videos.creator: City Steading Brews

findings.text: Foam and krausen can be normal early-fermentation behavior; contain possible overflow rather than treating foam alone as failure.

evidence.passage: They're going to create more foam ... this is not a bad thing ... put your new brew on a cookie sheet that has edges.

findings.text: A still airlock may reflect a poor seal; look for bubbles rising through the liquid and verify with gravity readings.

evidence.passage: Tiny bubbles ... means you have a fermentation that is active ... if your airlock isn't active, you could just have a bad seal.

findings.text: Replace or clean a clogged airlock and consider a blow-off tube during vigorous fermentation.

evidence.passage: Keep the one-way valve ... from getting blocked up ... that could cause some problems.

visual_review_needed: Visual examples of krausen, lees, and haze are important context.

videos.title: Allulose Stops Yeast? -Sweet, Bubbly, 14% ABV Mead
videos.creator: City Steading Brews

ingredients.original: 1/2 packet Mangrove Jack's M02 cider yeast

findings.text: They used non-fermentable allulose to retain sweetness while reserving measured sugar for natural carbonation.

evidence.passage: We want this to be sparkling ... didn't want to have to pasteurize ... we're going to be using allulose.
We now need 42 g of sugar ... a stable brew ... that's also sweet ... we want this to be bubbly.

findings.text: The finished batch was 1.026 and about 14% ABV, but carbonation was light rather than fully sparkling.

evidence.passage: This is 1.026 final gravity and 14%. Now this we sweetened with allulose.
It's carbonated. Not much. It's like petulant. Very sweet.

videos.title: Honeysuckle Mead -Easy Semi Sweet Mead without Pasteurizing or Stabilizing
videos.creator: City Steading Brews

findings.text: They deliberately step-fed past the stated yeast tolerance and observed a stable reading of 1.012 without pasteurization.

evidence.passage: It's sitting at 1.012 ... technically a step feed ... surpass the tolerance of that yeast on purpose ... so that you don't have to pasteurize.
Did it move in a week? If it didn't, that means it's stable ... always want to do two checks a week apart.

findings.text: The low pH may have contributed to the apparent stop, so the evidence does not prove alcohol tolerance alone caused stability.

evidence.passage: This sucker went down to 3.0 pH. That's probably why it stopped fermenting. That's a theory, hypothesis.

videos.title: OFFENSIVE Mead? - Step Feed Pyment Mead Recipe
videos.creator: City Steading Brews

findings.text: For step feeding, add only enough fermentable sugar that the batch would remain acceptable if fermentation stopped at that addition.

evidence.passage: Just in case it doesn't ferment anymore, you can still drink it and it's okay.
At what point would I be happy with it if it didn't ferment further ... I probably don't want to add anything more than a quarter pound.

findings.text: The staged additions fermented to 1.002 at the recorded checkpoint; the creators said the approach takes longer and still required later stability checks.

evidence.passage: It did actually ferment to 1.002.
Making a step feed takes longer ... if you like things dry you could just let this go another week.

videos.title: How to Make Mead - Dry Traditional Mead FULL PROCESS - 2024 Re-edit
videos.creator: City Steading Brews

findings.text: A quiet airlock is only a clue; verify completion with hydrometer readings.

evidence.passage: Neutral pressure in that airlock ... might be done. That's not a guarantee; it's just a sign.

findings.text: They state that a lower starting gravity is easier on yeast than overloading the initial must with fermentables.

evidence.passage: Using a lower gravity to start ... tends not to stress the yeast out as much ... overfeeding the yeast ... makes it really hard on your yeast.

findings.text: At roughly four weeks and 0.999, they described the dry mead as clean and strongly honey-charactered without sweetness.

evidence.passage: This doesn't [smell sulfury] at all ... smells very clean ... 0.999 ... bone dry ... I taste honey.

visual_review_needed: Confirm hydrometer reading shown on screen.

videos.title: This Mead Looked Disgusting... then THIS Happened: Apple Butter Mead
videos.creator: City Steading Brews

ingredients.original: 1/2 packet Mangrove Jack's M05 mead yeast

findings.text: They deliberately limited starting gravity to reduce the risk of a stall rather than relying on the yeast's maximum advertised tolerance.

evidence.passage: Don't count on it getting that high ... not be super high and cause a stall. We don't want our yeast to get concerned.

findings.text: After backsweetening, they pasteurized by bringing the liquid center to 160 F for one minute.

evidence.passage: Internal temperature, the middle of the liquid, to 160 F. We're going to hold it there for 1 minute.

findings.text: The final tasting reported apple, honey, and spice character; the spices came from the apple butter and oak rather than a separate spice addition.

evidence.passage: Apples and honey ... we did not add any spices ... spices that was in the apple butter and the spice notes that come from the amber oaking.

visual_review_needed: The unusually thick sediment and racking losses are strongly visual.
